critical_test_authority_is_forgeable.claim: CriticalTestExecutionAuthorityV1 accepts caller-supplied EXECUTED_PASS strings with no binding to a test run
critical_test_authority_is_forgeable.severity: HIGH - this sits at the authorization boundary
evidence: status_by_test is a plain Mapping[str,str] supplied by the caller
the ONLY status check is `if status != 'EXECUTED_PASS': raise` - it requires the caller to write that literal string, it does not verify anything ran
test_suite_source_sha256 is validated only for SHA-256 SHAPE, never against an actual suite
no junit, run digest, executed_at, report SHA or any other binding to a test-run artifact exists in the module
critical_test_authority_is_forgeable.consequence: even if all 33 roots were populated, issuance would NOT prove the critical tests ever executed; the authority records a CLAIM, not an EXECUTION
critical_test_authority_is_forgeable.this_is_the_pattern: a check that cannot fail, now located at the authorization boundary rather than in a test
critical_test_authority_is_forgeable.action_taken: REPORTED, NOT PATCHED - deciding what a valid test-run binding must be is an owner scientific/governance decision, and editing the gate to look stronger would be the same error this project has repeatedly warned against
